title: Prove exact cycle-constrained chart neighborhoods (no new κ)
body:
## Summary

Scoped all-dimensional geometry proof with exact finite corroboration: for any nonempty tuple of binary Lagrangian charts and a linear allowed-axis space A, the changed simultaneous transvection neighborhood has exactly

```text
I = intersection of the charts
B = A intersect I
m = dim A, b = dim B
t = rank of the pairing A -> B*
changed tuples = 2^(m-b+1) - 2^(m-b-t) - 1
```

The exact nontrivial axis fibers are `a + (B intersect a-perp)`. An executable coset construction returns one axis per changed tuple. Internal graph edges impose a linear cycle kernel, giving a complete neighborhood for coherent transported moves while preserving every internal contact rank. This extends David Ganz's PR4841 single/pair result; its unconstrained specializations are inherited.

Two explicit three-chart fixtures have identical pairwise distances but neighborhood sizes 63 and 47. A cycle restriction changes the latter count to 15. These distinguish the new tuple/intersection/pairing data from pairwise or unrestricted formulas. No new kappa or physical supplier is claimed. This contribution was produced by Nick Petalas. Credit David Ganz / Dugongue #4841, Cao Yifan / intqwq #4610, Cinna Davis #4690/#4672 and the retained native-caller lineage. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

## Evidence

- Before: PR4841 supplies unconstrained single/paired neighborhoods, without this allowed-axis tuple or cycle-kernel contract.
- After: literal subspace-image and exact-fiber checks pass all 226,260 ordered-triple/allowed-subspace cases through n=2. Another 4,096 literal axis tests cover 256 three-vertex, two-cycle graphs. The n=3 distinctions are checked separately. Eleven invalid-input controls and five named mathematical mutations reject.
- Both registered warning-strict ordinary and optimized checks pass locally on CPython 3.12, in 0.45 seconds each. These are local check durations, not a performance improvement. Package metadata/replay, exact committed-byte/source-history preflight and official committed-export integrity pass. A read-only, Git-free optimized copy replays with unchanged file hashes; altered source and receipt controls reject. RESULT.json is generated and bound to the package source hashes.

From the repository root:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/coherent-transvection-neighborhood/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -O -W error -B research/coherent-transvection-neighborhood/verify.py

/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/coherent-transvection-neighborhood --check-source-history
```

Expected direct output: `PASS_COHERENT_TRANSVECTION_NEIGHBORHOOD cases=226260 literal_graph_axes=4096`. A clean CPython 3.12 interpreter can replace the absolute local interpreter path. Standard library only. SOURCES.json pins canonical base `624de9dc66858af0945e5f8a0942488d62280d43`, priority revision 7, and the citation-only predecessor at `6debdcdac8fe1c87958f8cd42ccb7db73c0a0eef`. The predecessor is not imported or executed and no unmerged Git object is required for replay.

A fresh canonical fetch before submission found no guidance or source change. The final cached overlap scan covers 382 open PRs and 3,864 Discussion records; 6,233 tracked note paths are outside its sparse local scan. Distinctive terms were separately searched across main READMEs and merged PRs, and live claims/open work were refreshed. This coverage is not a novelty certificate.

The historical card positive control was attempted and raises `KeyError: 'complex_profile'` against the current selected schema. The current source-bound selected-baseline orientation passes. The old package is unchanged; its failure does not enter this proof or verifier.

## Limitations

The proof covers arbitrary n and tuple length. The reference enumerator explicitly bounds n<=9, charts<=64 and internal edges<=128. The graph result covers exact coherent edge conjugation, not every assignment preserving only edge ranks. Actual boundary-edge costs, absolute phases, independent dirty inputs, ownership, restoration, native realization, compiler/precision and outer admission remain open. No changed paid profile, complete multiplication theorem or selected-frontier change is supplied. No predecessor verification campaign, Lean, Docker, historical suite or selected cold replay was run.

## Open next questions

- Find one actual complete source word with a strict paid-moment gain from a cycle-coherent block move. Start with a small connected source contact subgraph, compute the cycle kernel and reprice every boundary edge and retained obligation.
- Classify rank-neutral coordinated moves outside exact edge conjugation. Start with one small cycle and compare all endpoint-axis assignments under an explicit replacement contract.

## Related open work

- #4841 supplies the inherited complete single/paired neighborhood theorem and native chart setting; this contribution adds restricted-axis tuples and exact cycle constraints.
- #4859 counts and indexes shortest literal axis words between two charts. That independent endpoint-word quantity differs from this simultaneous multi-chart output neighborhood; no numerical comparison is claimed.
- #4813 uses a small symplectic neighborhood in proposed five-array native ports. This contribution supplies no native port, completion or paid-schedule verification.

- #4866 gives a four-candidate concave pricing rule in the schematic full-subspace metric, with an explicit fixed-dimension/Lagrangian limitation. It does not count coherent chart-tuple outputs.
- #4861 classifies mixed-direction full-space Clifford batching. Its tensor-child similarity and directional multiplicities differ from the simultaneous chart fibers here; no common numerical value is compared.

Before DONE, this account's 10 open PRs created since the CLAIM at 2026-10-22 22:14:57 UTC were inspected for overlap, including this PR. The nearby chart-word, schematic subspace-pricing and mixed-direction results are distinguished above. None of the other submissions reports a competing cycle-constrained tuple count, and no extra predecessor computations were run.

## Merge danger
